page0.text:
It's 2:00 PM.
I make a late lunch and bring it to Sakura's room.

page1.text:
"...Okay."
I remove my apron and place a bowl of okayu on a tray.
I take one deep breath,
and completely still my heart.

page2.text:
I don't know what I'll say if I see Sakura in my current condition.
That wouldn't be good.
If she notices my inner turmoil, it'll make her suffer even worse than me.

page3.text:
I need to cool my emotions so that I don't say anything careless.
...This will probably be the last time.
It's our last chance to meet and look at each other, like we always have.
At the very least, I want this precious time to end with a smile.

page4.text:
"Are you awake, Sakura? I brought lunch. Sorry it's late."
I knock and enter the room.
Sakura looks like she was sleeping, but her face lights up when I come in.
"Yes! I'm glad you came, Senpai!"
She smiles warmly, looking genuinely happy.

page5.text:
...Time passes.
Sakura's body is on the mend.
She's well enough to sit up and eat her okayu on her own.

page6.text:
We spend lunchtime leisurely, chatting about nothing important.
Sakura goes back to her bed and continues talking to me. Maybe she's sleepy after eating.
That's all.
This is all I can do for her now.

page7.text:
Sakura looks lively now.
Her breathing is steadier now, and the color has returned to her cheeks.
I'd have a hard time believing someone who told me that she only has a few days left to live.

page8.text:
"I've never really caught a cold before, you know.
I've always had a good constitution, and I've certainly never been bedridden."

page9.text:
The topic turns from disliking cold medicine to Sakura telling me how healthy she normally is.
Apparently, she's never been a sickly person, and anytime she came close to catching a cold, she would overcome her symptoms through sheer willpower.

page10.text:
"By 'willpower,' do you mean staying warm and resting?
...No, that doesn't really capture the nuance of it, does it? How do you show willpower when you have a cold?"
"Uh, well... it's pretty embarrassing, so this is a secret."

page11.text:
Sakura gives me a rare shy giggle.
...Hm. It sounds like Sakura was a feisty kid in a different way than I was.

page12.text: "I don't dislike cold medicine so much as I don't really believe in it. Doesn't it make you nervous when you aren't sure if it's even working after you take it?"

page13.text: "Ahh, I did think that as a kid. When you drink that bitter stuff and you don't feel any better, and you get a fever and hurt all over, you start to wonder if it's the medicine's fault."

page14.text:
Sakura agrees enthusiastically with an "I know, right!?"
...Her smile is almost enough to make me imagine that she's well enough to be back on her feet tomorrow.

page15.text:
...
...I do my best to quash that wishful thinking.
Sakura won't get better.
I can't keep hoping that she'll get better and everything will go back to normal, and keep delaying my decision.

page16.text:
"...Hey, Sakura."
Maybe I ask this because I've accepted the cold, hard reality.
"Once you get better...is there anything you want to do?"
I start imagining what-if,
and ask her about fantasies of the future.

page17.text:
"Huh...? Something I want to do...?"
"Yeah. Things that you think are fun. It can be anything. I'm just asking, so it doesn't matter whether it's realistic."
"Uh... Hmm, give me a moment."
Sakura's gaze wanders, her face troubled.

page18.text:
She pauses to think.
"I don't think I've ever said this before, actually.
I think I'd be happy staying right here, as long as you're with me."
She answers shyly, her cheeks flushing.

page19.text:
...
My vision narrows.
I use my stilled heart to quash the urge to pick her up and hug her.

page20.text: "Until now, she has never acted in her own interests."

page21.text:
Damn that old man! It's not that she never tried...!
She just doesn't know!
She doesn't know what it means to do something fun.
She doesn't know what she wants because she's never lived a normal life.
She values the small things so much because she's never known normal happiness...

page22.text:
"...Senpai? Um, is something wrong?"
"Huh? Oh, I was just thinking about something."

page23.text:
She still hasn't done anything.
Sakura doesn't know what it means to aspire to something, or to feel the need to obtain something.

page24.text:
She doesn't laugh when she's outside.
She doesn't make friends.
She's only known closed-off spaces, like the Matou house and mine.
I'd pay any price to change that.

page25.text:
"S-Senpai? You're acting strange.
...Does your left hand hurt?"
"No, it's not that.
Sakura. Once this commotion is over, let's go someplace far away.
You've never taken a vacation anywhere, have you? It could be fun to go on a trip."

page26.text:
...
Sakura looks at me curiously.
Her surprised silence at my sudden suggestion gives the impression that she's wondering if this is a dream.

page27.text:
"It's decided, then. Where do you want to go?"
"Huh? Where? Um..."
She looks panicked.
She can't come up with an answer.
Still, perhaps she found a wish within herself.

page28.text:
"...Can it be anywhere?"
She timidly looks up at me.

page29.text:
"Sure. There's nowhere humans can't go when we set our minds to it."
I meant it seriously, but Sakura seems to have taken it as a joke.
She laughs.
"Then I'd like to go flower-viewing in the spring."
She voices a modest wish in a grateful tone.

page30.text:
"Flower-viewing? Like for hanami, during the cherry blossom season?"
"Yes. We could do it at this house, but all we have are plum trees. I want to go see the flowers with you in a big field on a sunny day."

page31.text:
"...All right. That does sound..."
Like an incredibly fun time.
It would be nice to go look at the springtime trees at the park under the bridge, on a bright blue day without any clouds.
There's countless fun things we could do.
Hanami would be a perfect first outing for Sakura.

page32.text:
"...Okay, it's a promise. Once you get better and this is all over, we'll go together."
Sakura flashes a contented smile.
We exchange a promise, and then I slowly stand up.

page33.text:
...Yeah.
It would be a dream come true if that could happen.
A dream of my own happiness, which I've never had ever since that fire ten years ago.

page34.text:
I leave the guestroom.
All that's left is that humble promise.
It isn't only Sakura's wish. It's mine, too.
Once April comes, I'll grant it as many times as it takes.

page35.text:
...
A warm illusion forms in my cold heart.
